An 8th State Pay Commission will be established without delay to provide salary hikes once the Central Government implements its new pay commission rates.
Priority will be given to noon meal workers, 108 ambulance staff, Anganwadi workers, and 1098 Mission Vatsalya staff for government job vacancies.
A new special pension scheme will be created for noon meal organizers, Anganwadi workers, fair price shop employees, and government employees who do not currently receive a pension.
Job security will be provided to noon meal workers, assistants, and Anganwadi workers under the Social Welfare Department.
Job security and salary regularization will be provided for Panchayat Secretaries and Village Assistants.
Job security will be ensured and salaries will be increased for sanitation workers in corporations, municipalities, town panchayats, and panchayats.
Employees of the Tamil Nadu State Rural and Urban Livelihood Missions will be enrolled under general and medical insurance schemes.
Police personnel will be provided with one day of leave per week on a rotational basis.
The washing allowance for police personnel will be increased from Rs. 500 to Rs. 1,000.
The food allowance for police personnel in other districts and corporations will be increased to Rs. 200, excluding Sundays.
Police welfare hospitals will be established in major cities including Madurai, Coimbatore, Trichy, Tirunelveli, Salem, and Vellore.
A special Anti-Drug Task Force will be established under the direct control of the Chief Minister to completely eradicate ganja and drugs in Tamil Nadu.
Medical help desks will be established in police residential complexes with a high number of residents.
A special insurance scheme will be implemented where the government will bear the full cost of life-saving surgeries for police personnel and their families.
A Police-Public Association will be formed under the leadership of a Deputy Superintendent of Police or Assistant Commissioner of Police to maintain good relations.
The uniform allowance currently provided to police personnel will be increased to Rs. 6,000.
Steps will be taken to increase the number of working days for Home Guards.
Government accreditation cards, medical insurance, and pensions will be provided without discrimination to local journalists, photographers, and registered web reporters at the taluk level.
Interest-free housing loans of up to Rs. 10 lakh will be provided through cooperative banks to accredited and long-serving non-accredited journalists for building their own homes.
The income ceiling for the journalist pension scheme will be removed.
Residential plots will be provided to journalists in major cities of Tamil Nadu to build houses.
The pension currently provided to journalists will be extended to visual media journalists.
The monthly pension will be increased from Rs 1,000 to Rs 2,500.
Under the 'Banker Bima Yojana' insurance scheme for handloom weavers, the death benefit for weavers dying before age 59 will be reinstated and increased from Rs 2,00,000 to Rs 3,00,000.
The Tamil Nadu Cotton Procurement Corporation will be established to procure and stock cotton during the production season to control yarn price hikes.
Free dhotis, sarees, and school uniforms provided by the Tamil Nadu government will be produced exclusively through weaver cooperative societies within Tamil Nadu.
The government will bear the insurance premium amount for textile workers.
Green houses integrated with weaving sheds will be constructed for the benefit of weavers.
A reward will be provided on the valuation of sarees woven by handloom weavers.
World-class government animal shelters and hospitals will be established in every district to rescue and care for stray animals.
A special sterilization program will be implemented to control the population of stray dogs.
The number of Christians undertaking the Jerusalem pilgrimage will be increased, and the financial assistance provided for the trip will be raised.
The number of beneficiaries for the Hajj pilgrimage will be increased and additional financial assistance will be provided for travel expenses.
Additional subsidies will be provided for the Umrah (Mecca-Medina) pilgrimage.
Land facilities will be provided for the construction of Christian cemeteries and Islamic burial grounds (Kabristan).
Firm action will be taken to retrieve Katchatheevu.
Family welfare funds will be provided to priests without discrimination and their pension will be increased.
Traditional folk arts like Salangaiyattam, Valli Kummi, Paraiyattam, Pambai Aattam, and Karagattam will be documented and promoted by the government.
World-class sports training centers and stadiums will be established in every zone.
Free sports equipment will be provided in panchayat areas to encourage the sports interest of youth.
The government will urge the establishment of a Supreme Court bench in Chennai.
The government will urge the Central Government to grant dual citizenship to Sri Lankan Tamil refugees living in India.
Travel concession fees will be increased for spiritual pilgrimages to Kailash-Manasarovar, Muktinath in Nepal, Haridwar, and the Vaishno Devi temple in Jammu-Katra.
The Annadhanam scheme currently implemented in temples will be expanded.
The government will urge the Central Government to expedite the caste-based census during the national census process.
A special committee will be formed to implement the RR Policy (Resettlement and Rehabilitation) for those who provided land for NLC.
Studies will be conducted to ensure a minimum monthly pension for EPS-95 pensioners who retired from private companies after 10 years of service, based on the models in Kerala and Puducherry.
A 1 percent reservation will be provided for the children of ex-servicemen for admission into undergraduate Arts and Science degree courses.
Compassionate appointments will be provided to the family members of soldiers who died or were disabled in the line of duty.
